mainTopic: Readiness of food on יום טוב (the תחום, trapped fish, זימון for an orchard animal) and slaughtering a dying animal on יום טוב
overview: The amud opens with the end of רב פפא's ruling: an item a non-Jew brings from outside the תחום on יום טוב is forbidden to the Jew it was brought for, but permitted to a different Jew. Next, רבה בר רב הונא quotes רב: fish found in a water channel that was dammed on ערב יום טוב are permitted. Someone learns from this that a wild animal nesting in an orchard needs no זימון. רב נחמן rejects this, because damming is an action while the orchard animal came on its own, and a ברייתא refutes the inference. A second ברייתא says the orchard animal needs no זימון. רב נחמן בר יצחק settles the clash: both ברייתות speak of a young animal, and the difference is whether the garden is near the city. A new משנה then teaches when a dying animal may be slaughtered on יום טוב, and how to bring meat home from the field. The גמרא quotes רמי בר אבא, who says meat should be skinned and cut up before eating. It then asks whether he is arguing with רב הונא, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: An item brought from outside the boundary: forbidden to one Jew, permitted to another
steps.stepSummary: The end of רב פפא's ruling: an item a non-Jew brought from outside the תחום is forbidden. But if it was brought for one Jew, a different Jew may use it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was brought from outside the תחום, it is forbidden. And an item that was brought for this Jew is permitted to a different Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רב פפא's ruling about a non-Jew who brings a gift to a Jew on יום טוב. If the gift came from outside the תחום, it is forbidden, but only to the Jew it was brought for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban falls only on the person the item was brought for. A second Jew, whom the non-Jew was not thinking of, may use it. So the ban depends on whom the item was brought for, not on the object itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside the boundary: the area beyond the distance a person may walk from his place on שבת or יום טוב
Forbidden
Permitted
A different Jew, not the one the item was brought for

steps.confusionAlert: The item does not become forbidden to everyone. It is forbidden only to the Jew it was brought for. Any other Jew may use it.

phrases.english: From outside the boundary, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: This picks up in the middle of רב פפא's ruling about a non-Jew bringing a gift to a Jew on יום טוב.

phrases.english: And what came for the sake of this Jew
is permitted to another Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב פפא's ruling from the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An item brought from outside the תחום is forbidden to the Jew it was brought for, but permitted to a different Jew.

steps.title: Fish found in a channel that was dammed before the holiday are permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא quotes רב: if someone dammed a water channel on ערב יום טוב and found fish in it the next morning, the fish are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of רב: If someone blocked off a water channel on the day before יום טוב, and the next day he got up early and found fish in it, the fish are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב about fish trapped in a channel that was blocked off before יום טוב. The fish may be eaten on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By damming the channel before יום טוב, the person shut the fish in ahead of time. So the fish count as caught and ready before the holiday began, and he does not have to trap them on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: One who dams or blocks off
A water channel, like an irrigation ditch
The day before the holiday
Fish

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section is built on this ruling of רב. Others try to learn a wider rule from it, and רב נחמן limits it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: הַסּוֹכֵר אַמַּת הַמַּיִם מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One who dams a water channel on the eve of the Festival,
and the next day he got up early
and found fish in it, they are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about animals and fish that were caught before יום טוב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fish found in a channel that was dammed on ערב יום טוב are permitted on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב חסדא learns: a wild animal nesting in an orchard needs no designation
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא learns from רב's ruling that a wild animal nesting in an orchard does not need זימון (setting it aside ahead of time) in order to be used on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: From the words of our teacher we can learn that a wild animal that nested in an orchard does not need to be set aside ahead of time.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא takes רב's fish ruling and widens it. He learns that a wild animal living in an orchard also counts as ready for יום טוב without being set aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's reasoning seems to be this: the fish were not set aside by name, yet they are permitted because they were already trapped. So an animal that nested in an orchard should also count as ready without זימון. This is an inference from רב's case to a new case.

keyTerms.meaning: From the words of our teacher (רב) we will learn
A wild, untamed animal
Nested, made its home
Orchard
Designating or setting aside an item before יום טוב so it can be used

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
From the words of our teacher we will learn:
phrases.notes: "Our teacher" here is רב, whose fish ruling was just quoted.

phrases.english: A wild animal that nested in an orchard
does not require designation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, מִדִּבְרֵי רַבֵּינוּ נִלְמוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new rule from רב's fish ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wild animal that nested in an orchard is ready for יום טוב without זימון.

steps.title: רב נחמן: Our colleague has taken on something too big
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rejects רב חסדא's inference, saying that his colleague has "fallen into a big matter", meaning he is reaching too far.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Our colleague has fallen into something big.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes back on רב חסדא's new rule. He is saying the inference is not so simple; the reason comes in step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Fell into a big matter" means רב חסדא stepped into a far-reaching question that cannot be settled by a quick comparison. רב נחמן does not yet say what is wrong. He only signals that the comparison will not hold.

keyTerms.meaning: Fell
Our colleague
Big, weighty matters

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Our colleague has fallen into great matters.
phrases.notes: It's a polite way of saying "he's jumped into a big, complicated issue", meaning the conclusion goes too far.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: נְפַל חַבְרִין, בְּרַבְרְבָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only רב חסדא's widening of the rule. רב's ruling about the fish still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not spelled out yet. It is explained in step 6.

steps.title: Another version: רבה בר רב הונא made the inference
steps.stepSummary: Some say it was רבה בר רב הונא, not רב חסדא, who learned the orchard rule from רב. רב נחמן then said "the son of our colleague" has fallen into a big matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבה בר רב הונא said, "From the words of our teacher we can learn that a wild animal that nested in an orchard does not need to be set aside." And רב נחמן said: The son of our colleague has fallen into something big.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same exchange. Only the speaker changes, and so does רב נחמן's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the inference comes from רבה בר רב הונא, the same man who reported רב's fish ruling. So רב נחמן calls him "son of our colleague", since his father רב הונא was רב נחמן's colleague. The content of the inference and of the rejection stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: The son of our colleague

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same exchange as steps 3–4, told with a different speaker.

phrases.english: Some say:
Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
From the words of our teacher we will learn:
A wild animal that nested in an orchard
does not require designation.
Rav Nachman said:
The son of our colleague has fallen into great matters.
phrases.notes: The "colleague" is רב הונא, so "his son" means רבה בר רב הונא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells steps 3–4 with a different speaker
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same inference as step 3, attributed to רבה בר רב הונא, and rejected the same way by רב נחמן.

steps.title: Why the comparison fails: in the channel case the person took an action
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains the difference. In the orchard the person did nothing, but in the channel case he took an action by damming it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There (the orchard), the person did not take any action. Here (the channel), he did take an action.
steps.whatsHappening: Here רב נחמן gives the reason behind his rejection. The two cases are different, so you cannot learn one from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fish count as ready because the person dammed the channel. That action before יום טוב trapped them, and it acts as his preparation. In the orchard he did nothing at all; the animal just came on its own. So רב's ruling cannot show that the orchard animal is ready without זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: There: the case being compared, here the orchard
Here: the case at hand, here the dammed channel
He is doing
An action

steps.whatToRemember: רב permits fish trapped in a channel dammed before יום טוב. You cannot extend this to a wild animal in an orchard, because damming is an action of preparation, while the orchard animal came with no action by the person.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a key idea: a physical action done before יום טוב can count as preparing something. Without such an action, something that merely happens to be in your area is not automatically ready.

phrases.english: There, he does not perform an action;
phrases.notes: "There" is the orchard case, where the animal came by itself.

phrases.english: here, he does perform an action.
phrases.notes: "Here" is רב's case: he dammed the channel.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא קָא עָבֵיד מַעֲשֶׂה, הָכָא קָא עָבֵיד מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רב נחמן's rejection in steps 4–5
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Shows that רב's fish ruling cannot be stretched to the orchard animal
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference ignores a key difference: damming is an action of preparation, while in the orchard the person did nothing.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the orchard animal does need setting aside
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges the idea that an animal nesting in an orchard needs no זימון by quoting a ברייתא that says it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it really not need setting aside? A ברייתא teaches: a wild animal that nested in an orchard must be set aside ahead of time. A free bird must have its wings tied so it won't be mixed up with its mother. This was a testimony given in the name of שמעיה and אבטליון.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן finishes his attack on the inference from רב's ruling. He quotes a ברייתא that says an animal in an orchard DOES need זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference from step 3 said an orchard animal needs no זימון. This ברייתא says the opposite in plain words. It also carries the weight of שמעיה and אבטליון, great early teachers.

keyTerms.meaning: Setting an animal aside before יום טוב so it is ready to use
An orchard
A free bird, a wild bird that does not stay in one place
A testimony, a teaching passed on from earlier sages
Two great early sages, teachers of הלל and שמאי

phrases.english: And it does not need setting aside?
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא:
A wild animal that nested in an orchard
needs to be set aside ahead of time,
and a free bird,
one must tie its wings
so that it will not be mixed up with its mother.
And this is a testimony that they testified
from the mouth of Shemaya and Avtalyon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב נחמן's rejection from step 6 with a source that proves his point.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that an animal nesting in an orchard needs no זימון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit ברייתא says such an animal does need זימון, so the inference contradicts a known teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wild animal nesting in an orchard needs זימון; a free bird needs its wings tied.

steps.title: The inference is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares that the inference from רב's ruling is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this round and says the inference drawn from רב has been knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the ברייתא clearly says the orchard animal needs זימון, whoever learned otherwise from רב's channel case was wrong. רב's ruling about fish in a dammed channel still stands; only the stretch to the orchard case falls.

keyTerms.meaning: A full refutation; the view has been disproven

steps.confusionAlert: What is refuted is the inference about the orchard, not רב's own ruling about the fish in the dammed channel.

phrases.english: A refutation.
phrases.notes: He means the one who learned the orchard rule from רב is proven wrong.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The inference that an orchard animal needs no זימון is rejected.

steps.title: A second ברייתא says the orchard animal needs no setting aside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the orchard animal really needs זימון, quoting a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר that says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it really need setting aside? A ברייתא teaches in the name of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that if someone set aside birds inside the nest and found them in front of the nest, they are forbidden. When is this said? With dovecote doves, attic doves, and birds nesting in jugs or a building. But geese, chickens, tame doves, and a wild animal nesting in an orchard are permitted and need no setting aside. A free bird must have its wings tied so it won't be mixed up with its mother.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns around and questions the ברייתא it just used. It quotes another ברייתא that says the orchard animal needs NO זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two ברייתות contradict each other: one says the orchard animal needs זימון, the other says it doesn't. The second ברייתא explains that זימון matters for birds that may fly off and be swapped, but tame animals and the orchard animal are permitted anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: A nest
A dovecote, a coop where doves live
When is this said? Limits a rule to certain cases
Tame doves raised in the house

phrases.english: But does it really need setting aside?
But wasn't it taught,
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:
Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel agree
about birds he set aside inside the nest
and then found in front of the nest
that they are forbidden.
When is this said?
With dovecote doves and attic doves,
and birds that nested in jugs or in a building.
But geese and chickens
and house-raised doves
and a wild animal that nested in an orchard
are permitted, and do not need setting aside.
And a free bird needs its wings tied,
so that it will not be mixed up with its mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a new ברייתא against the ברייתא from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא of step 7 that says the orchard animal needs זימון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different ברייתא explicitly lists the orchard animal among those that need no זימון, so the two sources clash.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Birds that might be swapped need זימון and are forbidden if found outside the nest; tame animals and an orchard animal need no זימון.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: tied and shaken birds
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא adds rules about birds marked by tying or shaking, where they are found, and stealing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Birds that were tied or shaken as a sign, if they are in pits, houses, ditches or caves, are permitted. In trees they are forbidden, because he might climb up and tear something off the tree. Birds tied or shaken by someone else are forbidden everywhere, because taking them is stealing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא from step 9. These are extra details about birds that were marked ahead of time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tying or shaking a bird is a way of setting it aside. Even so, if the bird is in a tree he may not take it on יום טוב, since climbing could lead to tearing off a branch. If someone else marked the bird, it belongs to him, so taking it is stealing.

keyTerms.meaning: Birds that were tied as a sign
Birds that were shaken or handled ahead of time as a sign
Lest he climb up and tear something off the tree
Stealing

phrases.english: And the tied ones and the shaken ones,
if in pits or in houses
or in ditches or in caves
are permitted,
but in trees they are forbidden,
lest he climb up and tear something off.
And the tied ones and the shaken ones
phrases.notes: Here it means birds that someone else marked.

phrases.english: are forbidden everywhere, because of stealing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the ברייתא begun in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marked birds in pits, houses, ditches or caves are permitted; in trees they are forbidden; birds marked by another are forbidden as stealing.

steps.title: One ברייתא is about the baby, the other about the mother
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן resolves the contradiction: the ברייתא that needs no זימון speaks of the young animal, the one that needs זימון speaks of its mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: There is no contradiction. This ברייתא is about the young animal, and that ברייתא is about its mother.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the clash between the two ברייתות. Each one is talking about a different animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The young animal cannot run away, so it is already as good as ready and needs no זימון. The mother is bigger and can escape, so she needs זימון. This way both ברייתות are correct.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
This one ... that one; each source is about a different case

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: It is not difficult:
This one is about it, that one is about its mother.
phrases.notes: "It" is the young animal that can't escape; "its mother" is bigger and can run away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each ברייתא is about a different animal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to discuss the same orchard animal and to disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The young animal needs no זימון; its mother needs זימון.

steps.title: Is setting aside enough for the mother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's answer: the mother can run away, so she should need real trapping, not just זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is setting aside really enough for the mother? She needs to be fully trapped!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב נחמן's answer. If the mother can escape, simply setting her aside should not be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that can run away is not yet caught, so using it on יום טוב would need a full trapping beforehand. That makes רב נחמן's explanation of the ברייתא that says the mother needs only זימון hard to accept. The challenge is not answered. Instead, the next step drops רב נחמן's answer and gives a new one.

keyTerms.meaning: It is enough
A full, proper trapping

phrases.english: For its mother, is setting aside enough?
She needs a full trapping!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's answer from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that the ברייתא requiring זימון is about the mother
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An animal that can escape is not yet caught, so it should need full trapping before יום טוב, not just זימון.

steps.title: Both teachings are about the young animal: near garden versus far garden
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says both ברייתות discuss the young animal. If the גינה is near the city, no זימון is needed. If the גינה is far, זימון is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: both teachings are talking about the young animal. One is about a garden near the city, and the other is about a garden that is not near the city.
steps.whatsHappening: The previous answer (young versus mother) was knocked down. So רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a new way to explain why one ברייתא needs זימון and the other does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother was the problem because she can run away. So now both teachings speak only of the young animal, which cannot escape. The difference is distance. Near the city, the owner always knows where it is and can take it any time, so no זימון is needed. Far away, he has to designate it beforehand.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is coming.
Both this one and that one
About it (here: the young animal)
A garden close to the city

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer: both ברייתות are about the young animal. Near the city, no זימון is needed. Far from the city, זימון is needed.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Both this and that are about it.
phrases.notes: "It" means the young animal, the one that can't run away, not its mother.

phrases.english: This one is about a garden near the city,
that one is about a garden that is not near.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב נחמן's answer, which was rejected in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by location (near garden versus far garden)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference between the ברייתות was young animal versus mother.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are about the young animal. Distance from the city decides whether זימון is needed.

steps.title: Slaughtering a dying animal on a festival
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a dying animal may be slaughtered on יום טוב only if there is time left in the day to eat a כזית of roasted meat. רבי עקיבא says time to eat a raw כזית from the neck is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If an animal is in danger of dying, a person may not slaughter it unless there is enough time left in the day to eat an olive-sized piece of it roasted. רבי עקיבא says: even enough time to eat an olive-sized piece raw, from the place where it was slaughtered, is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks when a person may slaughter an animal that is about to die on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slaughter must be able to count as being for the sake of eating on יום טוב. So the תנא קמא requires enough time to skin, roast and eat a כזית. רבי עקיבא is more lenient: time to eat a raw כזית from the neck area, without skinning or roasting, is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
An animal in danger of dying
Enough time left in the day
An olive-sized piece of roasted meat
From the place where it was slaughtered (the neck)

phrases.english: Mishnah: An animal in danger of dying — he may not slaughter it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ שְׁהוּת בַּיּוֹם
phrases.english: unless there is enough time in the day
to eat from it an olive-bulk of roasted meat.
Rabbi Akiva says:
Even an olive-bulk of raw meat from the place of its slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The זימון discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dying animal may be slaughtered on יום טוב only if a roasted כזית can still be eaten that day. רבי עקיבא says a raw כזית from the neck is enough.

steps.title: Bringing meat home from the field by hand
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: an animal slaughtered in the field on יום טוב may not be carried on a pole. It must be brought by hand, piece by piece.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered it in the field, he may not bring it home on a pole or on a set of poles. But he may bring it in his hand, limb by limb.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second rule about how meat slaughtered in the field may be brought home on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying a whole animal on a pole, or on poles carried by two people, looks like ordinary weekday work. So he must change the usual method and carry the pieces by hand, limb by limb.

keyTerms.meaning: A pole, and a set of poles carried by two people
Limb by limb, piece by piece

phrases.english: If he slaughtered it in the field,
he may not bring it on a pole or on a set of poles,
but he brings it in his hand, limb by limb.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחָטָהּ בַּשָּׂדֶה לֹא יְבִיאֶנָּה בְּמוֹט וּבְמוֹטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second ruling of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat slaughtered in the field on יום טוב is brought home by hand, limb by limb, not on poles.

steps.title: Proper manners: skin and cut meat before eating
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר אבא learns from the עולה, which had to be skinned and cut up, that butchers should do the same. From this the Torah teaches manners: do not eat meat before it is skinned and cut up.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רמי בר אבא said: skinning and cutting up is said about the burnt-offering, and the same is true for butchers. From here the Torah taught proper manners: a person should not eat meat before it is skinned and cut up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא on this משנה opens with a teaching of רמי בר אבא. It is a source the discussion will build on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah requires the עולה to be skinned and cut into pieces. רמי בר אבא applies the same practice to ordinary butchers. He calls it דרך ארץ, proper manners, not to eat meat before skinning and cutting it. This sits in tension with רבי עקיבא in the משנה, who allows eating a raw כזית straight from the neck.

keyTerms.meaning: Skinning and cutting into pieces
Burnt-offering
And the same rule applies
Butchers
Proper manners, good conduct

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a clash with רבי עקיבא's view in the משנה about eating raw meat from the neck before skinning.

phrases.english: Gemara: Rami bar Abba said:
Skinning and cutting up are said about the burnt-offering,
and the same is true for butchers.
From here the Torah taught proper manners:
that a person should not eat meat
before skinning and cutting up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא הֶפְשֵׁט וְנִתּוּחַ בְּעוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the new משנה and connects to the topic of eating meat right after slaughter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proper manners: meat should be skinned and cut up before it is eaten. This is learned from the עולה.

steps.title: What is רמי בר אבא teaching us?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new point רמי בר אבא's lesson adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what new point רמי בר אבא is making when he says meat should be skinned and cut up before eating. This question sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lesson about good manners seems obvious. So the גמרא wants to know if it carries a real legal point, perhaps one that argues with another אמורא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (What is the new point here?)

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, 'to exclude'. It shows up properly in the next line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the practical point of רמי בר אבא's lesson in step 16 is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new halachic point רמי בר אבא's lesson about skinning and cutting meat comes to teach.

steps.title: Suggestion: he argues with רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רמי בר אבא is arguing with רב הונא, who says a slaughtered animal is assumed permitted unless we know it became a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he comes to rule against רב הונא. רב הונא said: a live animal stays forbidden until you know how it was slaughtered. Once slaughtered, it is assumed permitted until you know how it became a טריפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer: maybe רמי בר אבא argues with רב הונא. It then quotes רב הונא's two-part rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא says a living animal is assumed forbidden until we know it was slaughtered properly. After proper slaughter it is assumed kosher, so it does not need checking for a טריפה. רמי בר אבא's demand to skin and cut up the meat first might mean he wants it checked, which would argue with רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (opens a suggested answer that may be pushed back)
To exclude, to rule out another opinion
Presumed forbidden
Presumed permitted
Became a טריפה, an animal with a fatal defect that makes it forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא has two separate presumptions. Before slaughter the animal is assumed forbidden. After proper slaughter it is assumed permitted. Do not mix them up.

phrases.english: If you say: to exclude the view of רב הונא,
as רב הונא said:
An animal, while it is alive,
stands in a presumption of being forbidden,
until it becomes known to you how it was slaughtered.
Once slaughtered, it stands in a presumption of being permitted,
until it becomes known to you how it became a טריפה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to step 17's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רמי בר אבא may mean to argue with רב הונא and require the animal to be checked before eating.

steps.title: But our משנה already agrees with רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: רבי עקיבא in our משנה allows eating raw meat right from the slaughter spot, which fits רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned our משנה like רב הונא! רבי עקיבא says: even a raw כזית from the place of slaughter. Doesn't that mean the actual slaughter spot?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the suggestion. Our משנה seems to follow רב הונא, so how could רמי בר אבא argue with him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא counts eating a raw כזית 'from its place of slaughter', meaning the neck. You could eat that right away, without skinning or checking the animal. That fits רב הונא's rule that a slaughtered animal is assumed permitted, so arguing with רב הונא would go against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn? (opens a challenge from a משנה)
Its place of slaughter
Is it not so that...? (pushing for a reading)
Actually, literally

phrases.english: But we learned our משנה in line with רב הונא!
As we learned, רבי עקיבא says:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה from step 14.

phrases.english: Even a raw olive-sized piece from its place of slaughter.
Is it not from its actual place of slaughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רמי בר אבא argues with רב הונא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lets you eat raw meat right from the slaughter spot without checking, which agrees with רב הונא. So arguing with רב הונא would go against the משנה.

steps.title: No, it means the intestines
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: 'בית טביחתה' can mean the place where the animal breaks down its food, the intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: No: it means from the place where its food is broken down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading רבי עקיבא's words differently. So the משנה does not prove רב הונא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'טביחה' means grinding up food, so the phrase points to the intestines, not the neck. The intestines can't be reached without opening the animal, so it still gets skinned and checked. The משנה no longer supports רב הונא, and רמי בר אבא can argue with him.

keyTerms.meaning: No (rejecting the proposed reading)
Where it breaks down its food, its digestive organs

phrases.english: No: from the place where it breaks down its food.
phrases.notes: This means the intestines, where food is digested. The same word can mean slaughtering or breaking something down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the משנה brought in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading of רבי עקיבא's words 'מבית טביחתה' as the actual slaughter spot.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase can mean the digestive organs, which need skinning and opening first, so the משנה does not support רב הונא.

steps.title: רבי חייא says it means the actual slaughter spot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading of 'בית טביחתה' as the intestines. רבי חייא's ברייתא says it is the actual place where the animal is slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי חייא teach: from the actual place where it is slaughtered?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from the last step. A ברייתא taught by רבי חייא clearly says רבי עקיבא meant the real slaughter spot, not the intestines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 the גמרא tried to avoid the proof by reading 'בית טביחתה' as the intestines. רבי חייא's word 'ממש' (actual) rules that reading out. So the original problem returns: רבי עקיבא allows eating right after slaughter, which fits רב הונא and goes against the idea that רמי בר אבא argues with him.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't someone teach (in a ברייתא)? An introduction to a challenge from a teaching
The place where the animal is slaughtered
Actual, literally

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Ḥiyya teach:
From the actual place where it is slaughtered?
phrases.notes: This is רבי חייא's version of רבי עקיבא's words in our משנה, and 'actual' blocks the intestines reading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rejection in step 20 by showing its reading of 'בית טביחתה' is wrong.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'בית טביחתה' as the intestines (step 20).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא's ברייתא says 'the actual place of slaughter,' so the intestines reading cannot stand, and רבי עקיבא again supports רב הונא.

steps.title: A new explanation of רמי בר אבא begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the idea that רמי בר אבא argues with רב הונא and starts a new explanation of his lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רמי בר אבא...
steps.whatsHappening: The word 'אלא' tells us the גמרא is giving up its earlier explanation. It is setting up a new answer about what רמי בר אבא really meant, which continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי עקיבא clearly fits רב הונא, the גמרא no longer wants to say רמי בר אבא disagrees with him. It goes back to the question of step 17, what רמי בר אבא adds, and starts a different answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals dropping the previous idea and offering a new one

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a complete statement. It only opens the new explanation, which finishes in the next lines.

phrases.english: Rather, Rami bar Abba

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 21 and abandons the answer of step 18, opening a new answer to step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point does רמי בר אבא's lesson add (from step 17)?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A new explanation begins here, replacing the claim that he argues with רב הונא; its content follows in the next lines.
